verdicts.title: Quantum communication complexity of linear regression
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Quantum computers may achieve speedups over their classical counterparts for solving linear algebra problems. However, in some cases -- such as for low-rank matrices -- dequantized algorithms demonstrate that there cannot be an exponential quantum speedup. In this work, we show that quantum computers have provable polynomial and exponential speedups in terms of communication complexity for some fundamental linear algebra problems \update{if there is no restriction on the rank}. verdicts.title: Lower Bounds for Approximating Graph Parameters via Communication Complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In a celebrated work, Blais, Brody, and Matulef developed a technique for proving property testing lower bounds via reductions from communication complexity. Their work focused on testing properties of functions, and yielded new lower bounds as well as simplified analyses of known lower bounds.
